audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Skill / Tryndamere / Tryndamere / Skill / Skill / Tryndamere / Tryndamere, which disagrees with the already-audited mirror.
audit.why: The mirrored garen__tryndamere audit set the chart to Garen, Garen, then Tryndamere for all five remaining stages, with ratings moved off 5/10 so the Tryndamere rows do not read as even. Garen genuinely owns levels 1-2: Decisive Strike is an 8s silence auto-reset and Tryndamere has no Fury banked yet.
audit.corrected: Garen, Garen, Tryndamere, Tryndamere, Tryndamere, Tryndamere, Tryndamere — proposed as one atomic full/content group with ratings.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level-6 spike had no cooldown numbers.
audit.why: Both ultimates are 120/100/80s. Courage is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s, Decisive Strike 8s flat, Judgment 9/8.25/7.5/6.75/6s.
audit.corrected: Both ultimates run 120s at rank 1; Courage is a 22s window at rank 1; 1v1 on Judgment's 9s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] said 'W slows him out of it' and mid repeated 'W-slow'. That is wrong twice: Mocking Shout reduces attack DAMAGE and its move slow only applies to enemies with their backs turned — and Decisive Strike explicitly breaks free of all slows.
audit.why: Riot's Decisive Strike text: 'Garen gains a burst of Move Speed, breaking free of all slows affecting him.' So neither Mocking Shout nor Stridebreaker holds him once Q is up. This is the decisive interaction of the matchup and it was absent.
audit.corrected: Decisive Strike breaks every slow on him — Mocking Shout and Stridebreaker will not hold Garen in place.

audit.whatIsWrong: Decisive Strike's auto-attack reset was never stated.
audit.why: The combo opens on the swing, not on a cast animation — the wind-up is the cue to step out.
audit.corrected: Step out on the wind-up, not the cast.

audit.whatIsWrong: Perseverance was never mentioned, and Demacian Justice's true damage was stated without the itemisation consequence.
audit.why: Perseverance only regenerates 'if Garen has not recently been struck by damage or enemy abilities' — one auto or Mocking Shout every few seconds denies it entirely. Demacian Justice being true damage means armour is not the answer to it; Undying Rage is.
audit.corrected: Chip him to deny Perseverance; answer the execute with R, not resistances.

edits.before: Level 1 is even, a skill check around his Q silence.
edits.after: Level 1 his Q silence out-trades your Fury-less body.

edits.before: Level 2 stays skill-based before you have full Fury.
edits.after: Level 2 he still wins short trades before full Fury.

edits.before: Once you have Fury you out-trade Garen: his Decisive Strike (Q) silence-hit is his only real burst, so bait it, then E in and Q crit while it's on cooldown. Bloodlust heals through his Judgment (E) spin, and W slows him out of it. Trade after his Q, not into it.
edits.after: Decisive Strike is an 8s auto-reset that silences — the wind-up is your cue to step out, not the cast. It also breaks every slow on him, so Mocking Shout will not hold him and the shout's slow needs his back turned anyway. Trade after his Q, never into it.

edits.before: Garen's Demacian Justice (R) is a true-damage execute on low targets, but Undying Rage makes you immune to it during ghost form. He wants to Q-silence, E-spin, then R your low HP — but your R denies the finish and Bloodlust refills. At 6 you clearly win the all-in.
edits.after: Demacian Justice is true damage, so armour is the wrong answer — Undying Rage is. Both ultimates run 120s at rank 1, so once he spends his on you and survives nothing, you own the next two minutes. He wants Q-silence into E-spin then the execute; deny the finish.

edits.before: Your crit item out-scales his bruiser build. Garen has no sustained damage once his E spin is healed off, while your crits shred him. Perma-shove, deny his passive regen by staying on him, and 1v1 whenever his Q is down.
edits.after: Your crit item out-scales his bruiser build. Perseverance only ticks when he has not been struck recently, so a single Mocking Shout or auto every few seconds shuts his regen off entirely. 1v1 him on Judgment's 9s cooldown.

edits.before: From level 3 on you take over. Your E-in, Q-crit, W-slow trade wins around his Q cooldown, Bloodlust heals through his spin, and at 6 Undying Rage negates his Demacian Justice execute. Force fights whenever his silence is down and you hold the edge.
edits.after: From level 3 on you take over. E in, crit, and heal his Judgment off with Bloodlust — but Mocking Shout cuts his attack damage, not his spin, and Decisive Strike breaks the slow anyway. Fight in his 8s Q window and at 6 through his execute.

edits.before: - Garen Courage: matchup-defining — Damage reduction on cast. Crit once it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Decisive Strike (Q): 8s — silence, auto-reset, and it breaks every slow on him. - Courage (W): 22s at rank 1 — shield plus brief tenacity, so crit after it lapses. - Undying Rage: 120s, and it answers his execute.

edits.before: Damage reduction on cast. Crit once it’s down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Courage is 22s at rank 1: shield, then tenacity. Crit after both have lapsed.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Courage's tenacity and shield eat your burst — wait the window out.

edits.before: Track Garen's Courage: Damage reduction on cast. Crit once it’s down. When it is down — Crit him down.
edits.after: Decisive Strike breaks every slow on him — Mocking Shout and Stridebreaker will not hold Garen in place.

notes: UNVERIFIED, left alone: whether Undying Rage can be cast while silenced by Decisive Strike. The Galio audit established that it casts through cast-inhibiting CC, but silence is a different category and the kit text does not settle it, so I did not write it. The existing spikes[1] phrase 'immune to it during ghost form' was left in place for the same reason — I replaced the sentence rather than sharpen an unverified claim.
